newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CPC CUTS PROPYLENE OUTPUT ON SLOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CPC CUTS PROPYLENE OUTPUT ON SLOW DEMAND.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday it was reducing propylene production at its Kaohsiung refinery by 30 percent due to sluggish demand from downstream petrochemical firms.
"Chinese Petroleum is cutting production on propylene in order to reduce inventory," an official told Reuters. "We have an overstock of propylene because downstream firms' demand remains slow."
The 30 percent cut included a 10 percent cut on August 8, officials said.
Chinese Petroleum's Kaohsiung refinery complex includes its third, fourth, and fifth refining units that can produce a total of 220,000 tonnes of propylene a year, official said.
The firm shut down its first refining unit in 1990 and closed its second in April 1994.
Chinese Petroleum had planned to move its second refining unit to Indonesia, but later cancelled the plan due to site selection problems.
